summary: Private deploy: corporate egress proxy strips Alt-Svc -> QUIC/HTTP3 bootstrapping fails, causing artifact fetch fallbacks and high retry rates
description:
Issue summary: Customers on a private VPC deployment report intermittent model shard download failures and elevated artifact retry counts. Root cause is suspected to be an on-prem/http egress proxy that removes or normalizes Alt-Svc / Alt-Used headers, breaking HTTP/3 (QUIC) bootstrapping advertised by our CDN. Impact: artifact retrieval falls back to HTTP/2 but the customer's proxy re-writes or blocks range/CONNECT behavior causing partial downloads, 502/416 errors and large numbers of retries. This increases inference latency and leads to failed in-flight requests for a subset of heavy model loads.

Impact: Several production customers experienced elevated 5xx error rates during model loads. One enterprise customer reported 25% increase in per-request latency for long-context generation during peak. No data exfiltration suspected.

Environment: Private deployment connected via VPCE to internet egress through customer-managed corporate proxy appliance. Observed only when the serving node egress path traverses the appliance; paths that egress via direct IGW do not show the failure.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private package in customer VPC with VPCE egress through corporate proxy appliance
2) Trigger large-model inference that requires sharded artifact downloads (models > 10GB)
3) Observe artifact fetch path from serving node to CDN; note any Alt-Svc header advertised by CDN responses
4) Simulate egress via the proxy using curl --http3 -v --resolve <cdn-host>:443:<cdn-ip> 'https://<cdn-host>/model-shard'
5) If proxy strips Alt-Svc or rewrites CONNECT, client fails to upgrade to HTTP/3 and fallback path encounters range/connection rewrites leading to 502/416 or truncated responses
expected_behavior: CDN responds with Alt-Svc that advertises HTTP/3 endpoint/token; client upgrades to QUIC and downloads shard successfully
If HTTP/3 is not available, fallback to HTTP/2 range requests should succeed without header rewriting or body truncation
actual_behavior: Alt-Svc header removed or normalized by egress proxy; QUIC token negotiation fails (QUIC_CLIENT_INITIAL_TOKEN_MISMATCH in traces)
Fallback HTTP/2 downloads encounter proxy-induced header rewrite or range merge that corrupts shard transfer -> 502/416 or truncated bodies
Large model loads trigger repeated retries and increased latency; some requests surface as 5xx in customer logs
logs: serving-node/http-client: WARN alt-svc header missing after egress: host=cdn.example-cdn.net, request_id=abc123
serving-node/quic: ERROR initial token validation failed: token=0x4fa2..., peer=203.0.113.42
cdn/access-logs: GET /models/shard-0001 range=bytes=0- ...  -> 200 with Alt-Svc: h3=":443"; ma=2592000
proxy/edge: INFO normalizer: removing header Alt-Svc for outbound responses to internal clients
comments: 2025-03-12 09:34 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports increase in 502s during model startup and attached serving node logs showing missing Alt-Svc. Asked for packet capture and proxy vendor config.

2025-03-12 11:02 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Ran curl --http3 test via customer-supplied jump host; observed Alt-Svc present upstream from CDN but response coming back through proxy had Alt-Svc removed. Captured TLS session metadata showing ALPN h2 only.

2025-03-12 13:54 - Customer (AtlasMetrics): Confirmed proxy appliance (AcmeSecure 7.2) has 'http.header.normalization.enabled=true' and default profile strips Alt-Svc/Alt-Used. Vendor suggested 'passthrough-alt-svc' option in advanced config.

2025-03-12 16:21 - Maya Chen (Support): Applied temporary mitigation path: toggled private deploy node config to force http2 (service config flag --force-http2-on-artifact-fetch=true). Observed downloads succeed with no header unmodified and no truncation. Customer confirmed progress but wants permanent fix.

2025-03-13 08:10 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Opened internal follow-up to add detection to Console (label 'alt-svc-stripped') and recommendations to Private deployment docs. Linked to SUP-809321 for tracking.
2025-03-13 12:40 - Customer (AtlasMetrics): Will test vendor suggested setting 'passthrough-alt-svc=true' in staging this afternoon and report results.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Corporate egress appliance was normalizing response headers and stripping Alt-Svc, preventing QUIC bootstrapping.
Hypothesis B: Some middleboxes rewrite Alt-Svc for privacy profiles and also rewrite byte-range headers on HTTP/2 responses, causing partial content to be rejected by artifact validation checks.

Packet captures: Downstream capture between serving node and proxy shows CDN response with Alt-Svc present; capture on outbound side of proxy shows Alt-Svc removed. QUIC Initial packet from client never reaches CDN when proxy is in path.
Reproduction: curl --http3 against CDN via direct internet path -> succeeds. Same curl via proxy -> fails to establish h3 and returns truncated body when forcing range requests.

Temporary mitigation success: forcing HTTP/2 on artifact fetch avoids broken QUIC negotiation and avoids proxy-induced range rewrite. However this increases tokenization/throughput inefficiency for some workloads.
Risk: Long-term forcing http2 globally reduces throughput and cost-efficiency; better to allow Alt-Svc to pass or to allow CONNECT/UDP passthrough for QUIC bootstrapping where possible.
Related signals: Increased artifact retry metric correlated with times when customer egress appliance updated signature rules (2025-03-11 03:00).
resolution_summary: Root cause: Customer egress proxy (AcmeSecure) was configured to normalize/strip Alt-Svc and to touch range headers, preventing HTTP/3/QUIC bootstrapping and corrupting range-based shard downloads. Immediate workaround: set private deployment flag to force HTTP/2 artifact fetch (--force-http2-on-artifact-fetch=true) or create an egress rule to route artifact CDN requests out IGW. Permanent fix: customer to enable passthrough of Alt-Svc (vendor setting 'passthrough-alt-svc=true') and allow ALPN passthrough / CONNECT UDP tunneling for QUIC token negotiation. SRE will add detection and a Console warning for 'Alt-Svc header missing on artifact response'. Follow-ups: Docs update and automation to prefer force-http2 only when proxy detected.
